items.text: Oman's Maritime Security Center announced on Friday, 8 Aban, that the country's navy evacuated 25 crew members of a commercial ship that caught fire after an attack. The ship "Riti" flying the Comoros flag was attacked 10 nautical miles off the coast of Musandam province, causing a fire on its deck. The evacuation operation was carried out with the cooperation of Oman's navy, and necessary medical services were provided to the crew.

Ali Salehi, the public and revolutionary prosecutor of Tehran, demanded the identification and blocking of pages of some unauthorized tourism tours and judicial action against their operators due to what he called "norm-breaking" and "publication of immoral content." He also emphasized the enforcement of mandatory hijab laws and called for security agencies to identify and confront what he named "organized gangs promoting and spreading corruption." Salehi further stressed increased supervision of businesses and public places and judicial action against citizens and business officials regarding dress code violations and what he termed "norm-breaking," actions that lead to expanded intervention in citizens' dress, lifestyle, and social activities.

Donald Trump and Melania Trump welcomed children dressed as cartoon and movie characters for Halloween at the White House. At the same time, a flyover demonstration passed briefly over the event location.

Mehdi Beigi, a member of the Iran International editorial team, commented on statements by Hossein Yekta, a commander in the IRGC, who said that people born in the 2000s are present next to missile launchers. He said the government tries to encourage teenagers to participate in the military and to put their education and knowledge at the service of military power.

Shahab Zahdi, a detainee from the January 2026 protests and imprisoned in Qezel Hesar prison in Karaj, was sentenced to death for the second time by Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. This sentence was issued after being overturned by the Supreme Court and the case was referred back for reconsideration. A source close to Zahdi's family confirmed this news.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said that the war with the Islamic Republic will end soon and that officials of the Islamic Republic want an agreement, but Washington needs a guarantee that Iran will never obtain nuclear weapons. He added that their leaders are so lost that we do not know who to negotiate with. Trump also emphasized that the Islamic Republic is the largest state sponsor of terrorism in the world and would use nuclear weapons if it obtained them.

Ali Shirazi, a member of Iran International's editorial team, mentioned the return of Qatari mediators to Tehran and said the Islamic Republic wants the negotiations to be limited to the Strait of Hormuz, but the US demands the complete dismantling of enrichment facilities.

Mayon volcano in central Philippines erupted on Friday, 8 Aban, sending a massive ash column into the air. Authorities raised the volcanic alert level to 3 and asked residents within a 6-kilometer radius to evacuate immediately due to lava flow danger.

Amirhossein Bankipour, a member of the Parliament's Cultural Commission, said revenge is a matter of belief and that ensuring the security of Iran and the world is not possible except through a firm confrontation and revenge against Trump and Netanyahu. He added that the official position of the Islamic Republic is that no negotiations will open until the US fully complies with Iran's seven conditions, and the Strait of Hormuz will remain as it is.

Turkey's National Intelligence Organization "MIT" arrested a Turkish national who was a member of ISIS in the Afghanistan-Pakistan border area and transferred him to Turkey. This individual, codenamed "Abdullah," had close cooperation with ISIS since 2024.
A 53-year-old woman was killed by her husband in Nishapur. The suspect was arrested by the police.

A released video shows the restlessness and expression of longing of the mother of the missing Peyman Pourdavarani due to the absence of her son. Peyman, 31 years old and father of a child, was killed on 18 Dey 1404 in Kerman.

Chelsea club faces a major deadlock after 15 years of unsuccessful efforts to build a new stadium with a capacity of 60,000 spectators. The project may cost up to five billion pounds, and the name of UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has been mentioned as a possible factor for progress. Chelsea has two main options: moving to the Earls Court area or rebuilding the Stamford Bridge stadium, but legal and structural obstacles remain.

Hojjat (Yaser) Moghadam, a resident of Birjand, was released on Thursday, 7 Aban, by posting a bail of four billion tomans from the Intelligence Department detention center in Birjand. This was reported by the HRANA news agency.

Saudi state media reported, citing informed sources, that the return of international inspectors to Iran's nuclear facilities will be a key point in potential talks between Tehran and Washington. Reuters also reported, citing an informed official, that Qatar's consultations to reach an agreement between Tehran and Washington are being coordinated with the US.

The Norwegian Foreign Minister warned about the increase in executions and the human rights situation in Iran, calling for a halt to executions and the release of prisoners. Interview with Mehran Abbassian, Iran International reporter.

Financial Times reported that the Islamic Republic used sticky mines in the attack on the oil tanker 'Louise 1' in the Strait of Hormuz. Two small vessels approached the tanker on Thursday evening and attached explosives to its hull. This is the first use of sticky mines against ships in the Middle East since June 2019.

Friedrich Merz, Chancellor of Germany, announced that the German government is coordinating and strengthening diplomatic efforts to end the Iran war as soon as possible. He emphasized that this conflict has no military solution and must be resolved through diplomacy. He also noted that the increase in energy prices over the past eight months has imposed costs exceeding 100 billion euros on Europe.

Farzin Nadimi, senior researcher for defense and security at the Washington Institute, referring to statements by Chris Murphy, US Democratic senator, about a possible plan to resume attacks on the Islamic Republic, said Trump is close to the final stages of decision-making, but diplomacy can still change this decision.

Heshmatollah Falahatpisheh, former head of the Parliament's National Security Commission, wrote on X that the shuttle diplomacy to Tehran is a definite sign of war, not the revival of diplomacy. He added that the situation has reached a stage where only a regional agreement involving the US and China can prevent the outbreak of a fourth war. Also, a Qatari mediator was present in Tehran on Friday, 8 Aban.

About 9 months after the issuance of the motorcycle license regulation for women, the training and issuance process has not yet started. This delay has deprived women applicants of formal training and legal and insurance support related to motorcycles. Women still face uncertainty, increased commuting costs, and the risk of imprisonment up to two months or fines for driving without a license.

Hassan Yazdani and Rahman Amouzad, Iranian freestyle wrestling representatives, won bronze medals by winning the classification matches at the World Wrestling Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan. Rahman Amouzad won 5-4 against Shamil Mamdov in the 65 kg weight class. Hassan Yazdani defeated Ahmed Tajdinov 5-0 in the 97 kg weight class and won the bronze medal.

Sergey Lavrov, Russia's Foreign Minister, arrived in Atlanta to attend the G20 Foreign Ministers' meeting. The meeting aims to prepare for the G20 summit scheduled for December 14 and 15 in Miami. The Russian delegation is also expected to hold several bilateral meetings soon, including with Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State.

Mike Pompeo, the US Secretary of State during Donald Trump's first presidency, said that resuming military operations against the Islamic Republic must lead to a resolution of the war and that this regime should not be allowed to rebuild its military capabilities. He also said the issue of the Houthis is not limited to Saudi Arabia and has regional and global dimensions.
A video sent to Iran International shows a poster with the image of Cyrus the Great and Prince Reza Pahlavi installed on one of the public passages in Tehran.

Alongside efforts to start peace talks between Russia and Ukraine, European countries are concerned about being excluded from the negotiation process. Europeans fear that the US and Russia will make decisions on important issues including European security and possible NATO restrictions in talks scheduled in Abu Dhabi within ten days, without their presence. Meanwhile, Russian drone attacks on a train station in eastern Ukraine have resulted in 14 deaths and several injuries.

Ali Alipour, the father of Babak Alipour, was transferred to Lakan Prison in Rasht after completing interrogation stages. This transfer took place on Thursday, 7 Aban. Harana News Agency reported this news.

Sepahan football team defeated Kheybar 2-1 in Khorramabad in the eleventh week of the Premier League and remained top of the table with 23 points. Kasra Taheri and Omid Noorafkan scored for Sepahan, and Amirhossein Farsi scored for Kheybar. In other matches, Malavan lost to Chadormalu Ardakan 2-1, and the match between Zob Ahan and Esteghlal Khuzestan ended goalless.

The G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, USA, began with discussions on global economic and geopolitical crises and their impacts on energy security, food, trade, and shipping. Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, said the world is at a "moment of choice" and called for member cooperation to strengthen economic resilience and protect markets. He also emphasized the importance of maritime and food security as foundations of economic security.

Safieh Sabzevari, a general practitioner residing in Sabzevar, was arrested 56 days ago on 14 Shahrivar after visiting the judiciary of the city and was transferred to Sabzevar prison. According to Harana News Agency, she remains in detention in Sabzevar prison. This doctor had previously been summoned to the judiciary to provide explanations.

Mark Carney, Prime Minister of Canada, announced during a meeting with Sheikh Khalid bin Mohammed Al Nahyan, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, that relations between the two countries have been elevated to a strategic partnership level with the signing of a free trade agreement and a $70 billion investment commitment. The leaders of the two countries issued a joint statement calling Iran's control over the three islands an "occupation" and demanded its end. In response, Esmail Baqaei, spokesperson for the Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, strongly condemned this stance and called the three islands an eternal part of Iran's territory.

Israeli forces blew up the homes of Palestinian families accused of carrying out a recent attack in the West Bank city of Hebron. In this attack, which took place on 22 October, two Israeli soldiers were killed.

Contrary to Iran's international commitments under the Convention on the Rights of the Child and obligations related to the non-use of children in military affairs, a group of female students from Isfahan county were sent to camps known as 'Rahian-e Noor'.
Videos received by Iran International show that a group of people in Vandadeh, Isfahan province, held a protest against mining activities and the destruction of natural resources.

People have reported that due to the economic crisis in Iran, essential medicines like rheumatism pills are unavailable and prices of goods have risen sharply. Store owners have reported a significant drop in sales due to inflation. Additionally, students complain about the high costs of books and exams, and pharmacies lack eye pressure medication.

Joachim Wadtfoll, Germany's foreign minister, said most G20 members want the Islamic Republic to return to the negotiating table. He added that the Houthis must stop their attacks and Russia must end its attacks in the Black Sea. Wadtfoll said G20 members are discussing crises and ways to restore the global economy to a growth path.

Maziar Zare, head coach of Malavan football team, resigned after a home defeat against Chadormalu Ardakan and said he will not return. Ashkan Pourrashid, owner and CEO of Malavan Bandar Anzali, opposed Zare's resignation and said he is talking to him to return. Malavan is in 10th place in the 11th week of the Premier League with three wins, three draws, and five losses.

Hassan Yazdani, the 97 kg freestyle wrestler of Iran's national team, after winning the bronze medal at the Astana Kazakhstan World Championships, said he is striving for the gold medal at the 2027 World Championships and the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. He told the Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting that his goal in this competition was another medal and he hopes to stand on the top podium at the 2027 World Championships and the 2028 Olympics.

Last week, reports covered live capture and trafficking of birds of prey, illegal hunting, wood smuggling, air pollution in several cities, reduction of dam reserves and groundwater resources, land subsidence, oak forest fires in Sardasht, and waste and sewage problems. These reports included discovery and seizure of live birds of prey, arrest of illegal hunters, confiscation of smuggled wood shipments, and unhealthy air conditions in several cities. Also reported were dam reserves reduction, warnings about land subsidence, containment of forest fires, and sewage discharge into rivers.
A worker in one of the units of Birjand Industrial Town died on the evening of Wednesday, 6 Aban, due to being trapped in a cardboard press machine.

Meir Javdanfar, an analyst of Israeli affairs, considered the possibility of annulment of the election results in Israel very low. He said there are different views regarding the accusation of foreign interference, and opposition parties and Netanyahu have requested the Shin Bet to investigate the matter.

CENTCOM claimed that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of Iran alleged today that it destroyed a US military unmanned vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, but CENTCOM called this claim false. CENTCOM stated that all surface unmanned vessels of the US military in the Middle East are present and their status is known, including a squadron of advanced unmanned vessels patrolling the Strait of Hormuz and supporting the US Central Command defense layer.
A probable timeline for the start of operations against the Islamic Republic and details of the first 24-48 hours of attacks have been reported.

Canada's intelligence and security agency announced that it has identified and thwarted several potentially deadly threats attributed to the Islamic Republic against individuals on Canadian soil. A spokesperson named the Islamic Republic and its proxy agents responsible for threatening opponents in Canada and said these activities will continue through 2026. The agency declined to answer specific questions about cases and continues cooperation with law enforcement and international partners to counter transnational plots.

The US Central Command, CENTCOM, called the IRGC report about the destruction of a US military drone in the Strait of Hormuz false and stated that the status of all US drones in the Middle East is known and none have been lost. CENTCOM wrote on its X social media account on Friday, 8 Aban, that the report of the drone's destruction, like many IRGC reports this week, is false. The command added that a unit of advanced US drones is patrolling the Strait of Hormuz and supporting CENTCOM's defensive posture.

Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, said the G20 must cooperate to address threats to the global economic order. He spoke at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta about disruptions in energy supply, food markets, supply chains, trade, and freedom of navigation. Experts and diplomats say deep disagreements over wars in Ukraine and the Middle East may prevent a joint statement at the two-day meeting.

Brad Cooper, commander of CENTCOM, said he did not see the IRGC forces while flying over the Strait of Hormuz and claimed the Iranian navy is "completely bottom of the sea." He claimed that US forces sank the Iranian navy earlier this year and cleared the main shipping routes of mines. Cooper also said that with an "iron siege of Iranian ports," they have prevented Iran from exporting even a drop of oil.

The Lithuanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that Iranian authorities have confirmed the detention of two Lithuanian women named Daiva Zakazauskaite and Erika Sleimaite, but the reason for their detention remains unknown.

Younes Khalifi, the creator of the controversial Mbappe meme about Mao Zedong, said he intended to travel to China and hopes they have no problem with him. He stated he never intended to upset the Chinese or Mbappe and would apologize if he meets Mbappe. The meme was created in summer 2023, and Khalifi never expected it to gain such a reaction.

Parsa Ghobakhloo, an undergraduate electrical engineering student at the University of Tehran, was expelled by the university's primary disciplinary council while retaining the right to participate in the entrance exam.

Mohsen Rezaee, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of the Islamic Republic, wrote on X that Europe until yesterday was proud of Israel's actions, but today complains about the billion-dollar costs of war with Iran. Rezaee, referring to what he called European countries' support for Israel's actions, asked if they did not think the consequences would affect them as well. He added that war has costs, and now it is Europe's turn to pay the price.

Shahriar Shams, an expelled student, has been held in Damghan prison without a clear decision for nearly three months. He faces charges including propaganda against the regime and assembly and collusion against national security, and his detention order has been extended. This was reported by Harana news agency.
Fardad Farahzad reported that negotiations among parties to form a coalition government in Israel have begun. This report was broadcast live from Jerusalem.

Ebrahim Rezaei, a member of the Parliament's National Security Commission, said that nuclear capabilities must be maintained at the highest level and uranium enrichment should be upgraded from 60% to 90%. He added that the nuclear industry has been a power factor in recent decades and that plutonium and enrichment at various levels are needed. Rezaei also said that at least 10 plans in parliament are proposed for exiting the NPT.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing the eternal grave of Naser Shirazi Karameh and said: "Here lies a hero. People, victory is near, do not despair." Naser Shirazi, 44 years old and fire and rescue commander, was killed on 18 Dey 1404 while helping protesters in Eslamshahr.

A diplomatic source said that Qatari negotiators have been present in Tehran and the negotiations lasted for 12 hours. The source added that Qatari mediators have been in regular contact with the White House throughout the day. The talks are still ongoing and efforts to reach an agreement between the US and Iran continue.

Jonathan Schaech, an analyst at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, said that correspondence with Mohsen Rezaee is likely Washington's last effort to achieve a diplomatic solution. He added that if the Islamic Republic does not return to negotiations, the US may launch a short but intense military operation against Iran after the midterm elections. Schaech also said that energy infrastructure and Islamic Republic officials may be targeted in future attacks, and the political crisis in Israel will not necessarily prevent military action.

Alireza Nourizadeh said Gulf countries are seeking international guarantees for their security amid a possible new confrontation with the Islamic Republic. He added that if the US and Israel launch extensive attacks on Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE might participate militarily. Nourizadeh also said regional countries are worried about repeated missile and drone attacks by the Islamic Republic.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said that negotiations with the Islamic Republic continue, but the US is not in a hurry to reach a result. He added that the Islamic Republic faces many problems and does not pay the salaries of soldiers and police forces. Trump also said this war is not an ordinary war.

Manshe Amir, a Middle East expert, said neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor Gadi Eizenkot can easily form the next government. He added that holding new elections will not necessarily change the result or end the political deadlock. According to Amir, forming a national unity government may be the only way for Israel to exit this deadlock.
A video released on social media shows a baker crying after sifting rationed flour in his bakery, telling citizens that instead of flour, animal feed has been delivered to bakeries.

Israeli media reported that Mossad has joined investigations into the case of foreign interference in the Knesset elections. Earlier, Shin Bet had started examining claims of foreign interference in the parliamentary elections. This report was by Ashkan Safaei from Iran International.

Turkic-speaking countries aim to expand strategic cooperation to increase their role in regional economic and security equations. The Organization of Turkic States, which began its activities based on historical, linguistic, and cultural commonalities, now has these cooperations on its agenda. The summit of the organization's leaders was held on Friday in Ankara.

Sepahan football team defeated Kheybar 2-1 in Khorramabad in the 11th week of the Premier League and became the league leader with 23 points. The team has had an outstanding performance in the last 6 weeks of the league.

Scott Busent, the US Treasury Secretary, said the US has taken action against banks worldwide to cut off financial resources to the Islamic Republic. He mentioned monitoring a large Pakistani bank, closing Dubai branches of an Egyptian bank, and shutting down a Turkish bank and Russia's second largest bank, VTB, due to dealings with Tehran. Busent said European banks are not a special weak point but one of many nodes identified through advanced monitoring.

On Saturday, 9 Aban, the football teams Nassaji Mazandaran and Persepolis will face each other in the eleventh week of the Premier League. Persepolis will become the leader again if they win this match.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International saying, "I have not received my salary for three months, but I am willing to endure these hardships so that the clerical regime of the Islamic Republic ends once and for all."

Danny Danon, Israel's ambassador to the United Nations, warned the representative of the Islamic Republic in his speech at the UN General Assembly that the Iranian government is on the verge of collapse and the Iranian people will soon have the opportunity to determine their own fate. He said the Islamic Republic had multiple opportunities to abandon its extremist ideology but rejected them all. Danon also called on countries worldwide to take a stand against the Iranian government and emphasized that Israel stands with the Iranian people.

Jamshid Barzegar said statements by parliament members and Friday prayer leaders about acquiring nuclear weapons are more of a propaganda campaign to pressure the US and the West. He added that threats have intensified with Mohsen Rezaei's increased role. Barzegar warned that leaving the NPT treaty would make support from Russia and China difficult and increase the risk of military attacks.

A Telegram channel close to the IRGC reported that eight oil tankers exploded in the Strait of Hormuz in the past 48 hours due to hitting mines. This channel is close to the IRGC and the statistics have not been independently confirmed. Earlier, the CENTCOM commander stated that American forces had cleared mines from the main shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz.
This Wednesday, the first women's football derby in Iran between Persepolis and Esteghlal was held; the Reds won this match.

Roghayeh Rezaei, a journalist and member of IranWire's editorial team, pointed to the overturning of Shahab Zahdi's death sentence by the Supreme Court and the reissuance of the sentence, saying that referring the case to the same branch and previous judge, instead of a peer branch, raises serious questions about the trial process. She also criticized the limited reactions of the international community to the increase in executions of protesters in Iran and called for practical measures to increase the costs of executions for the Islamic Republic.

Canada's intelligence and security agency announced it has prevented more than one deadly plot by agents linked to the Islamic Republic's intelligence services against individuals on Canadian soil. The agency warned that threats from the Islamic Republic will continue in 2026. Meanwhile, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police emphasized it is seriously pursuing cases related to the Islamic Republic's transnational interference and repression.

The Public Relations of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reported that on the evening of Friday, 8 Aban, the IRGC Aerospace Force grounded and captured an American MQM-170 reconnaissance drone using electronic warfare systems over Qeshm Island. The IRGC stated this is the second drone of this type their forces have captured. This claim has not been independently verified.

The Israeli army announced that Ihab Jamil Abutqiya and Ibrahim Jihad Muhammad Abu Asheiba, commanders of Hamas's military wing, were killed in an attack. According to the army, these two commanders had planned attacks on civilians and Israeli forces and were trying to rebuild Hamas's military capabilities. It was also reported that four other Hamas members were killed in southern Gaza and two weapons depots of the group were targeted in attacks.

Asharq Al-Awsat reported heavy clashes between Yemeni government forces and Houthis in the Al-Maqatra area, located north of Lahij province and south of Taiz. Houthi forces attacked government positions from three axes and tried to take control of Al-Maqatra. No confirmed casualty figures have been released yet.

Axios reported, citing diplomatic sources, that Qatari mediators' talks to reach an agreement on resuming direct negotiations between the US and the Islamic Republic will continue on Saturday, November 1, in Doha. Disagreements within Donald Trump's administration over the possibility of an agreement with the Islamic Republic persist. Egypt, Turkey, Iraq, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia have asked the Islamic Republic to agree to resume negotiations before the US midterm elections.

A Lebanese military court charged 13 people in the case of seizing a truck carrying half a ton of TNT and C4 explosives belonging to Hezbollah. The accused are charged with acting against internal security and illegal possession of weapons.

Shayan Samiei, a security expert, referred to the history of the Islamic Republic and the disputes between Tehran and Washington over the nuclear program and said he is not optimistic about a lasting agreement between the two sides. He emphasized that any limited understanding to stop the conflict, without imposing costs for violating the Islamic Republic's commitments, can only be a "band-aid" and provide an opportunity for the regime to regroup.

Omid Memarian, a political analyst, said that the idea of 90% enrichment or Iran's exit from the NPT is currently being discussed only among parliament members and hardline media and has not reached senior officials' decisions. He emphasized that Tehran's practical move towards 90% enrichment could create a new consensus for a military attack on the Islamic Republic and serve as Tehran's message to the US to increase the cost of any military action.

Ghassan Ashour, a Middle East analyst, said that the missile and drone attacks by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia are carried out more to increase economic and propaganda pressure on Riyadh than for military objectives. He also said that Houthi control over Taiz province could deal a heavy blow to the Saudi-backed government and further weaken its position in Yemen.
Turkey officially nominated Faridun Sinirlioğlu, the current Secretary General of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe, as its candidate for the UN Secretary-General position.

Hossein Alizadeh, an international affairs analyst, said that the accompaniment of a group of Iranian diplomats with the Qatari delegation to Doha could be a sign of limited progress in the dialogue process. He added that it is possible that a direct meeting between Iranian and American delegations could be arranged in Qatar, although there is still no clear information about the level of negotiations and potential concessions from both sides.

Several citizens in Mahdishahr were arrested and transferred to prison following the production and publication of a clip on social media. The head of the judiciary in this county stated that the location where the clip was produced has been sealed and its owner is under judicial prosecution.

Steven Daweti, the British Minister for Middle East Affairs, warned about the threats from the Islamic Republic against civilian infrastructure and shipping in the Persian Gulf, stating that Britain will not stand idly by against attacks on civilians, infrastructure, and commercial shipping threats. He emphasized that Britain stands with the people and the security of its regional partners and that Iran must not be allowed to acquire nuclear weapons. Daweti also said the Islamic Republic should not target partners, friends, commercial interests, and civilians.

Ali Motahari, the former deputy speaker of the tenth parliament, said Ali Larijani emphasized the necessity of negotiation even during war in their last meeting and believed negotiation during war could yield better results. Motahari also criticized opponents of negotiation and called for alternative solutions. He stressed that opposition without reasoning sacrifices the country's interests.
Afshin Azizi, a citizen from Urmia, has been arrested to serve a three-year prison sentence and transferred to the prison in that city.

Saeed Mehrzadi, Director General of the Inspection Office of the Food and Drug Organization, reported the identification of a pharmaceutical fraud worth 150 million tomans, in which the contents of the original medicine were replaced with distilled water. He said the vial belonged to another medicine that was emptied, filled with distilled water, and labeled as the intended medicine for sale as the original drug. Mehrzadi warned that buying medicine from cyberspace and unofficial markets can endanger patients' health.

A knowledgeable source told Iran International that Zeynab Soleimani, a pediatric specialist who has been held in Dolatabad Prison in Isfahan since Farvardin 1405, has faced severe mental health deterioration after months in solitary confinement and has been hospitalized three times at Farabi Psychiatric Hospital in Isfahan. The source added that Soleimani had no prior history of mental health issues before her arrest, but her condition worsened significantly during detention. Also, no trial has been held for this detained doctor so far, and there is no information about her possible charges.

Heavy rain caused by the remnants of Tropical Storm Wenceslas flooded the resort city of Los Cabos in Baja California Sur, Mexico, on Friday, 8 Aban. Vehicles and a bus were dragged to the beach, and several vehicles got stuck in the beach sand. A crane tried to remove the bus from the beach.
It was reported that seven workers were injured due to the overturning of a minibus carrying workers of the Morcheh Khort industrial town on the Shahin Shahr route in Isfahan province.

Alexia Putellas, former Barcelona captain and star of the Spanish national team, won the Ballon d'Or for the third time. She is playing this season for London City. Raha Pourbakhsh's report on Iran International examines what one of the highest-paid female footballers in the world is doing in English football.

According to reports, on the evening of Friday, 8 Aban, Basij and plainclothes forces clashed with young people gathered for a Halloween celebration in Iran Shahr streets of Tehran. Witnesses reported the arrest of two people, beatings of citizens, and closure of cafes. Families present in Honarmandan Park were also targeted by the forces.

Rouhollah Rahimpour said the Islamic Republic's threat of a harsh response to US attacks could be both a deterrent message and a sign of Tehran's concern about targeting senior officials. He added the Islamic Republic faces a time constraint to reach an agreement, while the US has more opportunity to apply pressure and set maximum conditions.

The commander of the Environmental Protection Unit of Khuzestan reported a shortage of personnel for protecting the natural areas of the province. Mohammad Alvandi said that 889 rangers are needed to protect 888,466 hectares of natural areas in the province, but currently only 220 rangers are responsible for protecting these areas.

Gholamhossein Mohseni Eje'i, head of the judiciary, called for faster handling of cases involving individuals he described as "spies," "enemy collaborators," and "traitors," stating that cases of those who acted against the country and the regime should be resolved sooner. He also emphasized dealing with these individuals with "full decisiveness" and "deterrent speed," remarks indicating a tougher judicial approach in security cases.

Fars News Agency reported that two boats in the waters of the Strait of Hormuz, about 14 miles south of Qeshm Island, were targeted by a drone attack, resulting in two missing and two injured. Fars wrote that these boats belonged to fishermen from the south of Qeshm Island and attributed the attack to the enemy. In recent days, attacks by the Revolutionary Guard forces on vessels have increased.

At the Manama security meeting, Bahraini officials warned about threats from the Islamic Republic and tensions in the region's waterways. Bahrain's interior minister called for strengthening security cooperation, and the country's crown prince emphasized international cooperation to secure the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab.

On Saturday, 9 Aban, calls for protest gatherings in 30 German cities have been published. More than 160,000 people are expected to participate in these gatherings. Opposition to the return of compulsory military service and protests against living costs are among the demands of the protesters.

Tractor club announced that Oman has not issued a direct flight permit from Iran, and the team members must travel indirectly to face Neftchi Uzbekistan in the Asian Elite League. The players and coaching staff will first travel to Istanbul and then fly to Oman. The Tractor supervisor said that if this situation repeats, the team will withdraw from the competitions.
A man accused of killing his 16-year-old son and mutilating his body was put on trial.

Mostafa Motadin, the new CEO of Esteghlal Club, considered the transfer of Esteghlal from Khalij Fars Holding to the private sector unlikely and said that the government has an interest in this team. He stated that in the long-term plan, he wants to make Esteghlal financially independent and work on broadcasting rights and sponsorship. Motadin added that he intends to turn fans from customers into partners of the club and if he stays for 5 years, he will make Esteghlal financially stable.

Reza Esmaeilpour, head of public places supervision police in Qazvin province, announced on Saturday, 9 Aban, the identification and sealing of 19 commercial units due to publishing content and images related to Halloween celebrations. This action was part of an intensified control and supervision plan aimed at combating the promotion of Western culture and lifestyle. The sealing of violating units and the formation of legal cases for offenders are underway by the police.

The media of the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic reported that Mojtaba Khamenei ordered in a meeting with senior commanders of the armed forces that any level and type of threat should be met with an "immediate, effective response without geographical limitation." Khamenei emphasized that if military attacks resume or officials are targeted, the armed forces of the Islamic Republic will determine the conditions for ending the conflict. He stressed strengthening military intelligence structures, developing defensive and security capabilities using new technologies, and enhancing indigenous defense in doctrine and tactics.

Mohammad Amin Valizadeh, head of West Azerbaijan University of Medical Sciences, announced that the hospital bed index in this province is currently 1.7 per thousand people, and to reach the national average of 2.2 per thousand people, 2000 new hospital beds need to be provided.

Mehdi Hasanpour, the public and revolutionary prosecutor of Yazd province, reported the closure of the venue for the Halloween party and the summons of the organizers in Yazd and Ardakan. He said that after receiving public reports, issues such as "unveiling" and mixed-gender parties were investigated, leading to the closure of the venue and summons of related individuals for investigation. Hasanpour emphasized that the public expects the judiciary to deal with such cases within the framework of laws and regulations.

The head of the Ferdis Chamber of Guilds reported the closure of one business unit in the county to prevent the holding and promotion of Halloween celebrations in cafes and similar places. Additionally, warnings have been issued to 30 other business units.

On Saturday, 9 Aban 1405, multiple messages from supporters of the Pahlavi family were published on the occasion of Prince Reza Pahlavi's birthday. Toshisuke Kanazawa, a 90-year-old Japanese bodybuilder, participated on Friday, 8 Aban, in the over-50 veterans bodybuilding competition in Santa Susanna, Costa del Maresme, Spain. He took part in the contest by following the same preparation steps as younger competitors, including training and spray tanning. Kanazawa aims to show that age is not a barrier to sports competitions and hopes to encourage others to maintain physical activity and challenge themselves in old age.
